blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In practice, the accounting equation is a constant quality check. Every transaction must leave the equation balanced. If you think a sale has only affected revenue, you have probably missed something — cash or receivables should have moved too.

Experienced accountants use this as a mental test. They ask themselves: "If I recorded this as only one side, what would the other side look like?" The question forces them to spot entries where something is hiding.

If the equation would not balance after your entry, the entry is wrong. That simple mental check catches hundreds of small errors before they become big ones — and it is the reason the equation has quietly survived for five hundred years.

items.q: According to the text, what must every transaction do to the equation?
items.why: "Every transaction must leave the equation balanced."

items.q: If a sale seems to have affected only revenue, the text suggests you have probably…
options: missed a movement in cash or receivables
items.why: "cash or receivables should have moved too."

items.q: What is the purpose of the accountant's mental test?
options: To spot entries where something is hiding
items.why: "The question forces them to spot entries where something is hiding."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Once the equation is out of balance, the entry is fine.
A quick mental check can prevent large errors.
Balancing both sides is a discipline worth keeping.
The equation still has practical value today.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz o contrário — "If the equation would not balance after your entry, the entry is wrong."

items.q: The phrase "quietly survived for five hundred years" suggests that the equation…
options: is rarely used in modern firms
has proven its usefulness over a very long time
items.why: Inferência: sobreviver cinco séculos como verificação indica utilidade comprovada e duradoura.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry orientando uma nova colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's look at these three entries together before you post anything. Take the first one — the cash sale. You recorded the revenue, which is right, but you stopped there. If you left it like that, the equation would not balance, because the cash that came in has to appear on the other side too. See? One side moved, so the other one must move as well.

Now the second entry. This is a sale on credit, so no cash yet. If you had recorded cash here, you would have been wrong — the customer hasn't paid. What moves is receivables, the amount they owe us. Always ask yourself where the second side is hiding.

And the third one. This looks fine on the surface, but if I recorded it as only one side, what would the other side look like? Nothing. That's the warning sign. Whenever only one side moves, something is missing.

Honestly, this little test takes five seconds, and it catches small mistakes before they turn into a week of detective work later.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was the problem with the first entry (the cash sale)?
options: The cash side was not recorded
items.why: "the cash that came in has to appear on the other side too."

items.q: Why would recording cash for the second entry have been wrong?
options: Cash is never recorded for sales
It was a refund, not a sale
It was a sale on credit and the customer hasn't paid
items.why: "This is a sale on credit, so no cash yet… What moves is receivables."

items.q: What is the "warning sign" Harry describes in the third entry?
options: Only one side moves and the other is empty
items.why: "Whenever only one side moves, something is missing."

items.q: What can we infer about Harry's approach to training?
options: He posts the entries himself to avoid errors
He teaches a quick habit that prevents bigger problems later
He thinks the mental check wastes time
He prefers people to learn only from written manuals
items.why: Inferência: ele mostra um teste de cinco segundos que evita uma semana de trabalho depois.

items.q: Which best describes Harry's tone with his colleague?
items.why: Inferência: ele explica cada entrada com calma e mostra o raciocínio — postura didática.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The invoice was sent, so we booked a receivable until the client pays." A receivable is…
options: an amount a customer owes us
items.why: Receivable = conta a receber: valor que o cliente ainda deve.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "After the correction, the ledger was fully ___ and both sides matched."
items.why: Balanced = equilibrado: os dois lados batem.

items.q: "A trained eye can spot a missing entry in seconds." To spot means to…
items.why: To spot = identificar, perceber algo rapidamente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A single missing figure can ___ the whole balance sheet."
items.why: To affect = afetar: influenciar o resultado.

items.q: "An error can hide on the second side of the entry." Here, to hide means the error…
options: is not obvious and easily overlooked
items.why: To hide = esconder: o erro fica oculto, difícil de perceber.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no dia a dia da contabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The senior accountant still has to sign off on the journal." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's double-check both sides before we post it." To double-check means to…
items.why: Double-check = conferir novamente para ter certeza.

items.q: "A small slip can turn into a week of rework." To turn into means to…
items.why: Turn into = transformar-se em, virar.

items.q: "We need to track down the entry that unbalanced the ledger." To track down means to…
items.why: Track down = rastrear até encontrar.

items.q: "Catching it early will save you a lot of trouble." To save someone trouble means to…
items.why: Save someone trouble = poupar alguém de dificuldade futura.
